thesis: Roku is under a definitive agreement (June 2026) to be acquired by Fox for $96.00 in cash plus 0.9693 FOX Class A shares per share, valued at $160 at signing; both companies' shareholders approved the deal on Oct 14, and closing is expected in 1H 2027 after a DOJ second request. At $160.08 the stock trades at about the headline deal value, which suggests upside is capped while an antitrust challenge would expose it to a large drop; today's 2.6x volume and new 52-week high are consistent with merger-arbitrage trading. Roku received Section 220 books-and-records demands and supplemented its proxy disclosures, and a Fox stockholder suit (Thompson v. Fox, Del. Ch.) challenged the deal disclosures; this run found no restatement.
invalidation: A higher competing bid, or the DOJ clears the deal and the stock trades meaningfully below deal value.
sources: SEC 10-Q (Roku, Section 220 demands and Fox suit): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001428439/000162828026054335/roku-20260630.htm

thesis: Qiagen agreed on Oct 21, 2026 to a cash takeover offer of EUR 46.50 per share from an EQT-controlled bidder (SC TO-C / SC 14D9-C filings), a 40.3% premium to the July 8 unaffected price, unanimously recommended by both boards, with committed financing, a 50%-plus-one-share minimum acceptance, an EGM vote and regulatory clearances, and closing expected in mid-2027. At $50.23 the stock trades about 4% below the offer at the roughly 1.125 USD/EUR rate implied by reported deal values, which suggests upside is capped at the offer price while a failed tender would expose it to a large drop; today's 13x volume is consistent with merger-arbitrage repositioning. Plaintiff firms opened investigations after the April 2026 QuantiFERON guidance cut, with no filed lawsuit found.
invalidation: A higher competing offer, or the tender fails to reach its minimum acceptance threshold.

thesis: Forgent fell about 21% today on 5.6x volume to a record low below its $27 IPO price after announcing that CFO Ryan Fiedler is stepping down to an external consulting role to spend more time with family, succeeded by EVP of Finance Amy Ard. The shares are down roughly 63% from their June peak even though the company reported record fiscal Q4 revenue and backlog and guided fiscal 2027 revenue of $2.4-2.6B (about 76% growth at the midpoint). The stated reason for the CFO change is personal and not tied to a disclosed operational problem, so it is not flagged, but the size of the selloff relative to the disclosed facts leaves the driver unresolved. The 200-day trend filter was skipped because the stock has traded only since February 2026, and the 10-Q reports only ordinary-course legal matters.
invalidation: A sustained recovery above the IPO price with confirmation that fiscal 2027 guidance is intact.

thesis: Waste Connections reported Q3 2026 on Oct 21 (8-K): revenue rose 7.3% to $2.638B, ahead of estimates, adjusted EBITDA reached $895.8M (34.0% margin) vs $830.3M, adjusted EPS was $1.58, and management raised full-year 2026 revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance for the second time while lifting the dividend 10% and buying back over $1B of stock year to date; the stock rose about 9.8% today on 2.9x volume to a new 52-week high. The fundamental counter-case is that growth is price-led, with same-store solid waste volumes down 1.2% against 5.5% core pricing, though the held margin and second guidance raise suggest pricing power is offsetting volume. However, a class action against Waste Connections subsidiaries over rate increases and fuel surcharges (D.S.C., No. 7:21-cv-02600) has a settlement final-approval hearing scheduled for Dec 7, 2026; the $1.4M amount is immaterial to the company, but it meets the active_litigation criterion, which caps this at low. Other matters (the Chiquita Canyon countersuit, in which the company is plaintiff, and an Avenal landfill residents' suit) have no scheduled dates found, and this run found no restatement or executive charge.
invalidation: Q4 results fall short of the raised outlook, solid waste volumes decline further without offsetting price, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$168.28).
sources: Open Class Actions (rate-increase settlement, Dec 7 hearing): https://openclassactions.com/settlements/waste-connections-rate-increase-fuel-surcharge-class-action-settlement.php

thesis: DexCom fell about 6.5% on Oct 21 and another 2.4% today on 3x volume after rival Abbott cut its diabetes-care outlook, which suggests a sector read-through on continuous-glucose-monitoring growth rather than a DexCom-specific disclosure; Q3 results on Oct 29 are a pending binary event. Positive items (G7 results in the CONNECT trial published in NEJM, target increases from Mizuho and BTIG) do not resolve that. A securities class action (S.D.N.Y., No. 1:25-cv-08912) over unauthorized G6/G7 design changes, following the March 2025 FDA warning letter, has no ruling date found.
invalidation: Q3 results on Oct 29 show U.S. CGM growth holding up despite Abbott's outlook cut, or an adverse development in the securities litigation.

thesis: Beacon Financial reported Q3 2026 on Oct 21 (8-K): net income of $0.73 per share and operating earnings of $0.77, short of the $0.78 Zacks estimate, with revenue also short, while net interest margin rose 4bp to 3.85% and the board raised its buyback authorization to $125M; management said borrower caution weighed on loan growth. The stock rose about 6.9% today on 2.8x volume, so the evidence is mixed: a modest miss offset by margin expansion and a larger buyback. A September 2025 class action (N.D.N.Y.) alleging Berkshire Bank aided a roughly $100M Ponzi scheme has no ruling date found, the August 2026 prospectus supplement was for subordinated notes rather than equity, and this run found no restatement.
invalidation: Credit deterioration or further loan-growth weakness in Q4, or a close back below the 200-day average.

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 19). AVTR set a new 52-week high of $17.45 intraday before closing about 0.7% lower, and this run found no new company disclosure; the thesis still rests on the Q2 2026 beat (adjusted EPS $0.21 on $1.69B revenue) and the raised full-year outlook, with analyst target increases (TD Cowen to $17). The counter-cases named in the prior thesis remain open: the motion to dismiss the securities class action is still being briefed with no ruling date, and Q3 results on Oct 28 are a pending binary event. Another law-firm investigation notice (Oct 22) adds no filed claim, so this stays medium.
invalidation: Q3 results on Oct 28 miss or guidance is cut, an adverse class-action ruling, or a close back below the 20-day average (~$15.68).

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 20). CLF fell about 7% today to $13.045 and JPMorgan cut its target to $12 (Neutral); this run found no company disclosure explaining the move, and the trading-blog reports attributing it to tariff pressure on the Stelco unit (idling of Hamilton Works cold-rolled and coated lines, Canadian government threats over layoffs) cite no primary source and appear to describe a late-September development. The thesis still rests on the Oct 19 Q3 report and the Q4/2027 EBITDA outlook, and the stock remains above the ~$12.12 pre-report level. The counter-case named in the prior thesis, the outlook's dependence on contract changes and steel-price forecasts, is still open, and the Stelco tariff and Canadian legal exposure adds to it, so this stays medium.
invalidation: Steel prices or contract pricing weaken enough to put the Q4/2027 EBITDA outlook at risk, a confirmed material Stelco shutdown or forced sale, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$12.12).
sources: StocksToTrade (Stelco tariff report, no primary source cited): https://stockstotrade.com/news/cleveland-cliffs-inc-clf-news-2026_10_22-2/

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 22). This run found no new company disclosure today; the thesis rests on the Oct 21 CLARITY-1/CLARITY-2 Phase 3 results, in which brepocitinib met the primary endpoint in non-infectious uveitis (Week 48 treatment failure about 35% and 32% vs about 78% on placebo, no new safety signals), and this run also found that brepocitinib (LISRAYA) has been FDA-approved and marketed for dermatomyositis since Aug 27, 2026, so an approved label already exists. The counter-case named in the prior thesis is still open: the uveitis sNDA is not planned until 1H 2027, so approval for this indication and its commercial weight within Roivant's portfolio remain pending, which keeps this at medium.
invalidation: Full CLARITY data or FDA feedback reveal a safety or efficacy problem, or a close back below the pre-announcement level (~$34.92).
